answer.text: show that molecules with nothing structurally in common produce the same state
answer.line: Right after the list, the author says these molecules share almost nothing, though drugs at one receptor usually share a shape.

steps: Ask why the list is there, not what is on it.
Read the line after the list: in any other drug class "the list would be absurd", since drugs at one receptor share a shape.
Sentence 7 lands it: "These share almost nothing beyond a mild reluctance to stay dissolved in water". Unlike molecules, one state.

choices.text: rank the agents by how safe each one is in practice
choices.note: Paragraph 8 describes shapes only. Safety comes up in paragraph 1, and no agent is ranked against another.

choices.text: show that molecules with nothing structurally in common produce the same state
choices.note: Unlike shapes, one state: the list makes the chemical variety impossible to miss.

choices.text: explain why the volatile agents became the most widely used members of the group
choices.note: No line says which agents are used most, or why.

choices.text: argue that only one drug on the list is a true anaesthetic
choices.note: Sentence 2 calls xenon a complete anaesthetic, and nothing in paragraph 8 rules a drug out. The list shows variety, not a disqualification.

choices.text: demonstrate that every agent named acts at the GABA type A receptor
choices.note: Paragraph 7 says ketamine, nitrous oxide and xenon leave GABA largely alone. The list mixes targets on purpose.

lockIt: Function of a list: read the line right after it. The author says there why the list is there.
